situation (example wording): "Tulsa, OK crime scorecard", "national crime scorecard", "Ohio crime scorecard", "Baltimore County, MD scorecard", "Anchorage scorecard"
what the app does today: The live (old) nibrsai.com answers these with a scorecard; the new engine answers them as a plain crime question or asks violent, property or both.
proposed behavior: "Scorecard" (also "scorecards", "score card", "score-card") is the live site's one-page scorecard, reproduced exactly: a table titled "<Place> Crime Scorecard (<year>)" (a county: "<County> County Scorecard (<year>)") with the columns Type | Offenses | Change from <prior year> | Rate per 100k | Clearance Rate, and nine rows in this order: Violent Crime, Murder, Rape, Robbery, Aggravated Assault, Property Crime, Burglary, Theft, Motor Vehicle Theft (Violent Crime and Property Crime are the totals, emphasized but not indented). The change column is each offense's percent change from the year before (blank, not 0, when the prior figure is missing or zero), the rate is per 100,000 of the agency's population, and the source is Crime Index. AN AGENCY (a city, or a county's one law enforcement agency) takes the latest year with complete crime, population and clearance data, and refuses a year more than 3 years behind the newest in the file; when the newest year fails the reliability check the card shows the latest reliable year and says the newer year may be incomplete. A STATE or THE NATION uses the FBI's own published state and national figures (Crime Index's state and national file), never a sum of agencies, in the latest FBI year, and has no clearance column (the FBI publishes no state clearance rate; the answer says so). A county with two agencies, or a name in two states, asks which one; no place named is the United States (P180). The whole card is one answer: no violent-or-property ask (P182's default is already the card's two totals). Any clearance rate above 100% carries the sentence that the FBI can clear cases in a year that originated in earlier years.
exact default or choices offered: The scorecard table, its title with the year, a status line ("<year> · Latest reliable year"), then the Source line.
why: Jeff 2026-11-22 (card through the coordinator): "Nibrsai does scorecards right now, recreate it" (the live engine's output is the specification: lib/agency-scorecard.ts, lib/historical-scorecard.ts, components/ScorecardPanel.tsx, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-agency-scorecard-panel-design.md).
status: Decided 2026-11-22 (Jeff, through the coordinator); build: Engine
test cases: Comes with the build (the 39 scorecard labels); the live builder's tests are the reference.
